Thanks for the ping, Rishi — quick read-through notes below. I attached our contracting checklist (redwood-contracting-checklist.pdf) for reference.

Clarifying Qs before we draft redlines:
1) Which Redwood legal entity should sign? If they want US entity, we'll confirm which entity ops prefers (usually Redwood Inference, Inc.).
2) Is Acme asking for EU residency for all data or only for records tied to EU customers? Please confirm — that determines if we need region-specific routing or a contractual data restriction.
3) Any negotiated commercial points already agreed (discount, committed throughput, burst allowances)? I know commercial mentioned a 10% introductory credit; confirm if that's locked.

Redline priorities and flags I will include:
- Data processing / DPA: require SOC2 + standard EU SCCs if transfers required.
- Sub-processors: we can provide a list and a notice process; we should avoid a clause that requires prior approval for every sub-processor.
- Indemnity / liability: push for our cap tied to fees; avoid unlimited indemnities.
- IP: retain our ownership of model weights and runtime; license customer data for service provision only.
- SLA credits: clarify measurement window and remedy process.

I can produce an initial redline using our template and a one-page summary of material changes by close of business Wed 11/04. If they need faster, I can do a prioritized checklist by EOD Mon 11/02.

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
